title: Choose the visual world for B-Anime
question: The roll assigned Broadcast Listings. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Broadcast Listings
options.lineage: Japanese newspaper TV listings (rate-ran) and weekly TV guide magazines
options.thesis: Your library is your own broadcast schedule: what's on next, set in a listings column rhythm with boxed state marks.
options.viewport: Left rail; 'Up next' as large episode cards; this week's airing shows set as a day-by-column listings grid with boxed NEW and FINAL marks.
options.risk: Boxed marks multiply into clutter if every card gets several. One mark per item, maximum.

raised.raise: Watched episodes are stamped, not hidden: the list keeps its history and shows what remains.
The library's A-Z jump rail sizes each letter tab by how many shows it holds, so 3,000 titles stay navigable.
One cell grid that every card, column and rule snaps to; no off-grid elements anywhere.
Every automatic status shows its evidence: 'Matched' shows the file, 'Synced' shows the AniList time.
Neutrals limited to a fixed stepped tonal ramp; no ad-hoc greys.

options.label: Obi Strip
options.lineage: the paper obi band wrapped around Japanese Blu-ray and manga releases
options.thesis: Every cover wears an obi band that carries its next episode and progress, coloured from its own key art.
materials: cover art as the only imagery
options.viewport: Left rail; 'Up next' covers, each wrapped by an obi showing episode number and a progress fill; library as a dense cover grid below.
options.risk: Cover-art-driven colour is the familiar fan-app look, and per-show colour can get loud across a full grid.

options.label: Streaming Title Wall
options.thesis: Rows of art; the one you land on grows and tells you what it is while the rest dims.
options.viewport: Continue-watching row up top, then horizontally scrolling rows; the focused tile expands with episode and progress.
options.case: Wins on product clarity (fans know it instantly), but it's a streaming service's identity, not your own collection's, and rows hide most of a big library.
options.risk: Reads as a streaming-service clone, and horizontal rows scale poorly to thousands of shows.

options.label: Jet-Age Ticket Wallet
options.thesis: Each season as a coupon book, one leg torn off per episode.
options.viewport: A wallet of episode coupons per show.
options.risk: Travel metaphor fans don't identify with.
options.case: Loses both axes: no fan identification, and coupons are slower to scan than a list.

options.label: Acetate Tab Manual
options.thesis: Sections as tabbed dividers with acetate leaves.
options.viewport: A stepped tab rail down the edge.
options.risk: Reads as documentation, not a media app.
options.case: Loses both axes: no fan identification, and the reading-first type fights a media grid.

options.label: Crouwel Grid Specimen
options.thesis: The visible grid as the design.
options.viewport: Huge grid-built titles over a visible grid.
options.risk: A poster aesthetic that buries cover art.
options.case: Loses both axes: competes with the artwork the product exists to show.

options.label: Monochrome Product Canon
options.thesis: Every claim paired with the interface detail that proves it.
options.risk: Cold and corporate for a fan app.
options.case: Loses both axes: a marketing form, and cold for fans.

options.label: Darkroom Exposure Record
options.thesis: Translucent sheets over an eleven-step zone ramp.
options.risk: Hatching and overlays fight cover art and add clutter.
options.case: Loses both axes: photographer's world, and visually busy.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark anime media app the way Crunchyroll and Plex ship it, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Big banner of the current show, continue-watching row, then library grid.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other anime app by design.
